arn.text: Night, the male speaker of the poem, and Day invite each other to a festival and trade stories, promises and gifts before their parting, and on their last day together they walk across the Daraja Plains, seeing everything as children.

Day recalls herding sheep with Night as children, and Night remembers Day's sacred rites, from which she returned a warrior with a tattooed eye, until Day announces she must leave tomorrow to war, promising to return and telling Night to wait for her.

Day tells of a time when, with a magician's help, Time was stopped and Night wrapped Day in his cloak and the two became as One, until Night was pulled away by the western horizon, and she concludes that they must live apart, glimpsing each other only across the sky, because neither can change.
